section_title: What do the two sticks becoming one mean?

versions.label: BSB
paragraphs: 15 Again the word of the LORD came to me, saying, 16 “And you, son of man, take a single stick and write on it: ‘Belonging to Judah and to the Israelites associated with him.’ Then take another stick and write on it: ‘Belonging to Joseph—the stick of Ephraim—and to all the house of Israel associated with him.’ 17 Then join them together into one stick, so that they become one in your hand. 18 When your people ask you, ‘Won’t you explain to us what you mean by these?’ 19 you are to tell them that this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘I will take the stick of Joseph, which is in the hand of Ephraim, and the tribes of Israel associated with him, and I will put them together with the stick of Judah. I will make them into a single stick, and they will become one in My hand.’

20 When the sticks on which you write are in your hand and in full view of the people, 21 you are to tell them that this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘I will take the Israelites out of the nations to which they have gone, and I will gather them from all around and bring them into their own land. 22 I will make them one nation in the land, on the mountains of Israel, and one king will rule over all of them. Then they will no longer be two nations and will never again be divided into two kingdoms. 23 They will no longer defile themselves with their idols or detestable images, or with any of their transgressions. I will save them from all their apostasies by which they sinned, and I will cleanse them. Then they will be My people, and I will be their God.

context_lines: Ezekiel is told to write on two sticks, identifying one with Judah and its companions and the other with Joseph, Ephraim and its companions. He is to join them so that they become one in his hand.

When the people ask the meaning, the Lord explains it. He will gather the Israelites from the nations and make them one nation in their land, with one king. They will no longer be divided into two kingdoms.

The reunion includes cleansing from idols and rebellion. Becoming one is not simply putting two names on a shared territory; the Lord will save and cleanse the people so that they belong to Him as their God.
common_interpretation_lines: [Henry](https://biblehub.com/commentaries/mhc/ezekiel/37.htm), [Wesley](https://biblehub.com/commentaries/wes/ezekiel/37.htm) and the [USCCB notes](https://bible.usccb.org/bible/ezekiel/37) understand the joining as the uniting of Judah and Israel. Wesley connects their becoming one in God’s hand with His government, care and blessing.
The passage supplies the explanation of the action. The joined sticks point first to the divided people being gathered and made one under the Lord’s rule.
god_plan_lines: [Ephesians 2:11–22](https://biblehub.com/bsb/ephesians/2.htm) develops a further work of unity through Christ. Jews and Gentiles are brought near through His blood, reconciled to God in one body, and given access to the Father by one Spirit.

This is a broader connection, not a replacement explanation in which one of Ezekiel’s sticks secretly means the Gentile church. Ezekiel names Judah and Joseph; Paul describes the peace Christ makes across another division. Both direct attention to a people united by God’s saving action and living in His presence.
